pubmed._query_note: ANCHOR LIST, 2026-08-17. The pan-tumor terms above (PD-L1, pembrolizumab, nivolumab, atezolizumab, durvalumab and the EGFR/ALK/KRAS biomarker strings) are AND-ed to this anchor because alone they match any tumour type. Measured on 2026/07/31-08/10 the anchoring drops 359 of 857 candidates, and 357 of those 359 are correctly dropped: mostly other primaries carrying lung METASTASES, plus mesothelioma, SCLC and pulmonary carcinoid. Precision is not the problem here. WHY THE PLURALS ARE SPELLED OUT: PubMed does not stem inside a quoted phrase, so the singular phrase does NOT match 'lung cancers'. That cost exactly one real paper in the window measured (PMID 42582901, on strengthening EGFR blockade for those lung cancers that need it most). Adding the plural recovers it: +1 paper, and that paper is the genuine one. MEASURED AND DECLINED at the same time, 2026-08-17: "lung tumor" and "lung tumour"[Title/Abstract]. Attributed term by term on 2026/07/31-08/10, "lung cancers" recovers 42582901 and pulls no noise; "lung tumor" pulls PMID 42485616 (murine patrolling monocytes, not lung cancer) and recovers nothing; "lung tumour" matches nothing either way. All three together scored 502 against 501 for the plural alone, so the two tumor spellings were pure cost in this window. They are speculative insurance against a phrasing that did not appear, and are left out until a window shows them earning their place. Do NOT replace any of this with bare lung[Title/Abstract]: measured, that recovers 15 papers of which 14 are other primaries with lung metastases. DO NOT DROP THE Title/Abstract ANCHOR IN FAVOUR OF THE MeSH TERMS ALONE. 48% of a fresh 10-day window has no MeSH assigned yet, so a MeSH-only anchor scores WORSE than this one (489 vs 499 on the same window). MeSH rescues old papers; it cannot anchor new ones. CONSIDERED AND DECLINED 2026-08-17, SELF-ANCHORING THE LUNG-EXCLUSIVE AGENTS: osimertinib, alectinib, lorlatinib and afatinib are effectively lung-only (measured noise in the dropped set: osimertinib 0, alectinib 1, lorlatinib 1, afatinib 2, against pembrolizumab 72, nivolumab 53 and PD-L1 192). Letting those four match with no anchor would recover the slice this query does lose: NSCLC drug-safety, adverse-event case reports, regulatory notices and editorials, which name the agent but never the indication (measured 21/60 -> 35/60 on a drug-led-title corpus set). DECLINED because that slice is weak signal for KOL identification, and widening the main query is the wrong instrument for it. If it is wanted it should be a deliberate SECOND query with its own tagging, so those papers stay distinguishable from the primary corpus instead of being blended into it. Do NOT self-anchor sotorasib or adagrasib in any such query: KRAS G12C is approved in colorectal and studied in pancreatic, and both pulled non-lung papers in testing.
